newsitem.title: USA: Sterling Bancorp sees 20 pct earnings gains.
newsitem.headline: Sterling Bancorp sees 20 pct earnings gains.

text.p: Sterling Bancorp, a New York-based banking and financial services company with $850 million in assets, is confident it can continue to post 20 percent-plus quarterly earnings gains in line with its performance over the last 14 quarters, president John Millman said in a telephone interview.
Earlier Wednesday, Sterling reported fourth-quarter net income rose 47 percent to $2.35 million.

Fourth-quarter earnings per share rose 24 percent to $0.31 per share. Millman said in the year-ago quarter there was a lower number of shares outstanding, about 6.4 million, compared to the 7,683,190 shares at the end of the latest period. The increase reflected the company's move to call two series of high-priced subordinated debt, which prompted the holders to convert to stock.
Millman said his confidence in continuation of 20-pct plus earnings growth applies to both net income and earnings per share.
In addition to its banking businss, Sterling is involved in factoring, leasing and investment management services.

In loans Sterling targets the low end of the middle market, specifically loans in the $500,000 to $10 million range. Millman said Sterling's niche lending business has benefited from consolidation of larger banks in New York.
Sterling also seeks to handle the personal banking business of entrepreneurial owners of mid-sized businesses.

The businesses are often private companiese such as architects, lawyers and accountants. Millman believes Sterling's New York City business has benefited from a big pickup in the local economy which he attributes to "a percerption that the quality of life in the city is much better."

Although Sterling has a relatively low return on equity, 13.21 percent at the end of the fourth quarter, Millman noted that it has risen from the 10 percent area a year ago and the goal is to get it to 15 percent or higher in 1997.
